title: National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 — Jurisdiction, Relief and Principles

content.overview: The National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 establishes a specialised tribunal for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources. Section 14 confers jurisdiction over civil cases involving a substantial question relating to environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I. Section 15 empowers the Tribunal to provide relief and compensation to victims of pollution and other environmental damage, for restitution of property and the environment. Section 20 directs the Tribunal to apply the principles of sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle while passing any order or decision or award.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Substantial environmental question from Schedule I enactments? (2) s. 14 jurisdiction? (3) Relief/compensation under s. 15? (4) s. 20 principles applied?
content.study:
NGT is the primary statutory forum for many environmental civil disputes. Constitutional writs remain available where maintainable; do not collapse NGT and High Court routes.

No new case invented. Doctrinal principles in s. 20 link to Vellore and related holdings already retained in doctrine topics.

sections.heading: s. 14 jurisdiction
sections.body: Civil cases involving a substantial question relating to environment arising out of implementation of Schedule I enactments (including EPA, Water Act, Air Act and others as listed).

sections.heading: s. 15 relief
sections.body: Relief and compensation to victims of pollution and environmental damage; restitution of property and environment.

sections.heading: s. 20 principles
sections.body: Tribunal shall apply sustainable development, precautionary principle and polluter pays while passing orders, decisions or awards.

sections.heading: Limitation
sections.body: Application within the period prescribed in the Act from the date on which the cause of action first arose (check current text for exact period and condonation).

sections.heading: Appeal
sections.body: Appeal to the Supreme Court as provided in the Act.

examples.title: Industrial pollution claim
examples.body: Victims of industrial discharge affecting water and soil approach NGT under ss. 14–15 seeking compensation and restitution; Tribunal applies s. 20 principles.

hypotheticals.question: Must every environmental dispute go only to the High Court under Article 226?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Where the dispute falls within s. 14 and Schedule I, NGT is the specialised statutory forum; writ jurisdiction is a separate maintainability analysis.

distinctions.title: NGT statutory jurisdiction vs High Court writ
distinctions.left: s. 14 civil environmental questions from Schedule I statutes; s. 15 relief.
distinctions.right: Article 226 constitutional jurisdiction — maintainability and alternative-remedy tests apply.

misconceptions.trap: NGT can decide any civil dispute involving the environment without a Schedule I link.
misconceptions.correction: s. 14 requires a substantial environmental question arising out of implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I.
